S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.

subtypes.Skin Defects: Excessive preoccupation with practically invisible acne, scars, or complexion.
subtypes.Facial Features: Preoccupation with the shape or size of the nose, eyes, or mouth, which appear normal to others.
subtypes.Asymmetry: Excessive obsession with the face or body not being perfectly symmetrical.
subtypes.Muscle Dysmorphia: The belief that one's body is too small or insufficiently muscular despite being normal or muscular.
subtypes.Specific Body Parts: Obsession that specific parts like hair, teeth, or chest are ugly or abnormal.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.

subtypes.Mirror Checking or Avoidance: Compulsively checking oneself in the mirror frequently or, conversely, avoiding mirrors strictly.
subtypes.Excessive Camouflaging: Spending excessive time and effort to hide perceived flaws using makeup, clothes, hats, or sunglasses.
subtypes.Skin Picking: Picking or manipulating the skin excessively to remove or 'fix' flaws.
subtypes.Reassurance Seeking: Repetitively asking others for confirmation that one's appearance is okay or not strange.
subtypes.Comparing: Constantly comparing one's body parts with those of passersby or celebrities.
subtypes.Seeking Cosmetic Procedures: Repeatedly seeking or receiving plastic surgery or dermatological procedures.

symptom.disease_info: Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD) is characterized by a persistent preoccupation with perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are either not observable or appear slight to others, leading to significant distress or impairment. Individuals commonly engage in repetitive behaviors (such as mirror checking, grooming, or seeking reassurance) or mental acts in response to their concerns. Onset is typically in adolescence or early adulthood and the course is often chronic, with symptoms waxing and waning around stressors, interpersonal situations, and appearance-related events. BDD is distinct from normal appearance concerns and from eating disorders in that the focus is on specific perceived defects rather than weight/shape globally, and from psychotic disorders in that beliefs, while sometimes overvalued, are usually not frankly delusional across contexts.

patient.personality: James is a steady, service-oriented man who is thoughtful, dutiful, and tends to internalize stress while trying to be reliable for others.
patient.stressor: In his mid-50s, James went through a period of health challenges, including weight fluctuation and treatment for a minor cardiac issue, which led to more frequent medical visits and advice about lifestyle changes. Seeing himself in clinic mirrors, patient portal photos, and ID badges after these changes, he began to fixate on specific aspects of his appearance that he felt made him look unwell or "damaged," and he compared himself harshly to old family photos he used in his genealogy hobby. Working in a customer service role where he is face-to-face with people all day and informally mentors younger staff, he started to feel that his perceived physical "defects" undermined his authority and the calm, competent image he prided himself on projecting. Over time, these worries began occupying more of his mental space at work and home, causing him to avoid certain social situations and feel increasingly distracted and exhausted, prompting him to seek psychiatric help after his spouse pointed out how much of his free time had become consumed by brooding over and trying to "fix" how he looks.
patient.chief_complaint: “I can’t stop zeroing in on what’s wrong with how I look since my health issues, and it’s really wearing me down.”

S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.
S067.manifestation: Ever since those heart appointments, I can’t look at myself without fixating on how sunken and unhealthy my face looks, like my eyes are too baggy and my skin has this gray, damaged look that makes me seem older and sicker than I am, especially when I compare it to the old family photos I use in my genealogy stuff where I looked strong and solid.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.
S068.manifestation: I catch myself constantly sneaking into the restroom at work to study my face in the mirror, adjusting my glasses and combing my hair just so to try to hide the lines and sagging I see, and then at home I’ll zoom way in on my ID badge and portal photos on my phone, asking my wife and even my younger coworkers over and over if I look “worn out” or “off” compared to everyone else.
